meaning: From Squalus: Latin squalus, “dirty” or “filthy” (squalid), an ancient name for marine fishes considered unfit for human consumption, including sharks; -idae “family of”
description: Slender dogfish sharks with a pointed snout, a spine in front of each of the two dorsal fins and no anal fin. The family has two living genera, Squalus and Cirrhigaleus.
